tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

borle-sim-scope: Section 3, p.8: the authors state their aim (preliminary insight) and the sizes used (12x12 data, 4x4 and 6x6 biclusters).
borle-sim-setup-noiseless: Section 6, p.15: classical computers, Perceval and Strawberry Fields, all simulations noiseless; stated as the paper's own setup.
borle-sim-simplified-heuristics: Section 6, p.16: four problems on 12x12 data and simulations based on a simplified version of Algorithms 1 and 3, stated by the authors.
borle-gbs-even-dimension-limit: Section 5, p.15: the authors call the even-dimension result the major restriction of GBS and say odd N or specific b1 x b2 shapes need post-processing.
borle-non-overlapping-scope: Footnote 19, p.15: the work deals only with non-overlapping biclusters; overlapping needs a more refined approach, as the value says.
borle-no-hardware: Section 7 item 2, p.27: 'At the time of writing, there was no publicly available hardware that would support problems of the sizes like the ones in this work.'
borle-quardp-definition: Section III-A, p.4: Equation 11 is the paper's QuarDP objective; Dirac-3 variables map to elements of W and H; zero-coefficient slack variable added, as the value says.
borle-qubo-quadratization: Section III-B, p.4 and Contribution 2: binary approximation then quartic to quadratic reduction with penalties; make_quadratic() of Ocean SDK named.
borle-variable-count-formula: Section IV, Eq. 18, p.4-5: the 39-variable machine limit gives p(n+m)+1 <= 39, with the slack variable explained in the text.
borle-setup-hardware-software: Section IV, p.5: 10 runs per case, i5-1335U laptop with 32 GB, scikit-learn v1.3.1, Or-Tools v9.14.6206 as stated.
borle-real-nmf-factor-range: Section IV, p.5: real test cases use W, H in [0,1) to suit Dirac-3; the scaling remark is stated in the same passage.
borle-exp1-setup: Section IV-A1, p.5: sizes 1 to 4 square, n=m=p, 100 cases each, rand() rounded to hundredths, 5x5 would exceed 39 variables.
borle-exp1-schedules-and-R: Section IV-A1/A2, p.5-6: schedules 1,2,3; R = p(n+m) = 2n^2 because no value in W or H exceeds one; run time set by qci_client. All stated by the authors.
borle-exp1-comparison-protocol: Section IV-A1, p.5: lowest-error Dirac-3 run against scikit-learn defaults with NNDSVDA; relative Frobenius error (Eq. 19-20).
borle-exp2-setup: Section IV-B1, p.6: V in R^(4x8), W 4x3, H 3x8; test set A random V, test set B V = WH, as the value says.
borle-exp2-exact-factorization: Section IV-B1, p.6: set B is built as V=WH so an exact factorization is guaranteed by construction; none is guaranteed for set A.
borle-exp2-variables-schedules: Section IV-B1, p.6: 37 variables, 10 runs, schedules 1 and 2; schedule 3 skipped for long run times.
borle-fusion-protocol: Section IV-B1, p.6: the three-step fusion procedure (median-energy run, decode W and H, use as W0 and H0 for sklearn defaults) is the paper's own definition.
borle-binomial-test: Section IV-B2, p.6-7, Eq. 21: one-sided binomial test, H0 and H1 as stated, p<0.05 threshold.
borle-exp2-percent-decrease-definition: Section IV-B2, Eq. 22, p.7: the metric and its range (-inf,100] with negative meaning an increase are defined in the text.
borle-exp3-setup: Section IV-C1, p.8: 100 cases per n in 1..4, entries 0 to 7, V=WH, QUBO two levels, QuarDP eight levels, schedule 1.
borle-cpsat-objectives-and-protocol: Section IV-C1, p.8: Eq. 23 and 24 objectives, ten runs, single processor in performance mode, time limit set to Dirac-3 time, best of ten kept.
borle-exp4-setup: Section IV-D1, p.9: rectangular 4x8 integer V, test set A random, test set B V=WH with entries 0 to 7.
borle-exp4-protocol: Section IV-D1, p.9: median runs compared, schedule 1, CP-SAT time matched, serial and 12-processor parallel configurations.
borle-future-work-limits: Section V, p.11: the authors list five directions they leave for future work (regularization, hybrid method, all-optical vs parallel CP-SAT, energy analysis, better integer NMF domains); the value matches the list. What the paper does not cover.
borle-ai-declaration: AI Declaration Statement, p.12: the authors state the LLM uses (grammar, CP-SAT starter code later verified by the authors, curve fits for Figure 3b).
borle-code-data-availability: Code and Data Availability, p.12: the authors give the repository (underscore lost in the text layer, shown as 'NMF NVN'). A statement about the paper's own materials, not a result.
borle-39-variable-limit: Section IV, p.4: 'Dirac-3 machine can have up to 39 variables for a quartic objective function [45]. Therefore ... we are limited to 39 variables.' The limit on the paper's own experiments is stated.
bose-setup-dataset-task: Section III.A and IV: Titanic dataset, features normalized to [0,1], label Survived or Not Survived.
bose-setup-model-optimizer: Section III.B and III.F: ZZFeatureMap, hardware-efficient ansatz, Qiskit Estimator, MSE loss, COBYLA.
bose-setup-execution-mode: Table 1, p.6: statevector for ideal and shot-based sampling for noisy; shots fixed per experiment; seed fixed.
bose-setup-dataset-noise-levels: Section IV.A.a, p.6-7: sigma 0.05, epsilon 0.05, impulse ratio 3%, dropout 0.05, step pi/255, as listed.
bose-setup-angle-noise: Section III.D, p.4 and Section IV.A.b, p.7: angle mapping, zero-mean Gaussian noise, wrapping to [-pi,pi], sigma values 0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05.
bose-setup-circuit-noise-levels: Section IV.A.c, p.7: depolarizing 0.05, amplitude and phase damping gamma 0.05, Pauli error 0.02.
bose-setup-circuit-configs: Section III.E, p.4: four independent binary noise sources give 2^4 = 16 circuit configurations including the baseline.
bose-limit-dataset-scope: Section VI, p.9: the authors name the Titanic testbed and leave harder datasets for future work. They state it as a scope limit.
bose-limit-unmitigated-no-scale: Section VI, p.9 and V.G, p.9: the work focuses on unmitigated noise and the experiments do not directly probe large-qubit systems.
bose-reproducibility-seeds: Section IV.A.d, p.7 and V.F, p.9: fixed seeds for split, noise and initialization; identical COBYLA stopping criteria; CSV logs supplied.
bose-limits-simulation-only: Section VI, p.9: 'limited to small-scale quantum circuits' and 'relies on high-fidelity noise simulation ... validating on real quantum hardware remains an important direction for future work.'
thm-iii-4-total-gamma-bounded: Section III A after Eq. 32, p.6: the condition bounds the total gamma angle, so for large p the theorem misses the optimal-angle regime (conjectured gamma_tot = Theta(p)). The authors state it.
thm-iii-4-energy-only: Section III A, p.6: 'the result only shows closeness of the QAOA energy density to the quantum annealing one, and makes no claim about the closeness of states.'
def-iii-1-discretization: Definition III.1, p.5 (Eq. 15 to 18): gamma at the left end of each interval, beta as the interval average, as the value says.
def-sk-model: Definition II.1, p.3: SK cost function with i.i.d. N(0,1) couplings and its qubit encoding.
qgms-energy-representation: Proposition C.1, p.27, derived in Appendix C 1 (path integral and Gaussian integration by parts); the paper says it reproves the earlier result for completeness.
saddle-point-existence: Propositions D.7 and D.8 (Appendix D 2, p.42): conditions given in Eq. D46 and Assumption 1; proved in D 2 b (convergence and analyticity) and D 2 c (solves the saddle-point equation).
sk-qgms-sufficiently-small-gamma: Appendix E 3 b, p.101: Eq. E202 to E205 check the Proposition D.7 smallness condition for the SK-QAOA QGMS (c_min = c_max = 1) and give gamma_max below an absolute constant. A short derivation in the paper from a proved proposition.
prop-e19-continuum-g2: Proposition E.19 (p.108): the bound holds for gamma_max below an explicit multiple of 1/c, c an absolute constant (E255, E263); proof p.109-110 (uniform bound, continuity, Lipschitz). The discrete bounds are proved by 'adapting' the proof, which is brief. The reader's concern (garbled bound) is a text-layer issue; the proof is in the paper.
prop-e23-e25-discretization: Propositions E.22 to E.25 (p.114-120): each has a proof in Appendix E 3 c (E.22 p.115, E.23 p.115 to 117, E.24 p.118, E.25 p.119 to 120). The discrete bound of E.22 is by 'replay' of the E.19 proof. Conditions on gamma_max are stated qualitatively as in the value.
cor-e28-qgms-moment-bounds: Corollary E.28 (p.124): bounds hold for gamma_max below an absolute constant; short proof from E.26 and E.27 bounds and counting of matchings.
proof-sketch-other-contributions: Appendix E 2 (end, p.89), Appendix E intro (p.79) and Appendix F intro (p.125): the authors state which parts are treated in full and which are sketched. This is the passage that limits the proof of Theorem III.4.
lemma-f16-annealing-average-exists: Lemma F.16 (p.148-149): proved by dominated convergence with a union-bound domination argument (Eq. F246 to F253). The state limit (F242) rests on a standard Euler/Trotter argument noted in Eq. 25.
weakness-gamma-bound-concentration: Appendix F 3, p.147: 'a major weakness of our results is the requirement of an absolute bound on the continuum gamma schedule magnitude'.
trotter-step-limit-total-time: Sections III E and IV, p.16: the authors say the theory does not predict how the Trotter step varies with total evolution time and the constant may need to decrease; numerics suggest otherwise.
scope-sk-and-constant-time: Section IV, p.16: 'our proof techniques are restricted to the SK model and constant total evolution time'; the generalization is only expected.
numerics-setup: Figure 1 caption (20-spin SK), Figure 8 (n from 10 to 20) and Appendix A 1: start from p0 = 17 infinite-size optimized angles of Ref. [12], Fourier extrapolation to larger p.
numerics-metric-residual-ar: Section III B, p.8: relative residual approximation ratio (AR_QAOA - AR_QA)/(1 - AR_QA), motivated by both algorithms nearing the exact solution.
qaoa-qa-limitation-smooth-angles: Section IV, p.17: 'An important limitation of our findings is their restriction to gradually varying QAOA angles.'
bowles-def-noncontextual-ontological-mod: Definition 2.0, Section 2.6, p.9: the triple, constraints (16) and (17), and the reproduction of P(E|S) by Eq. 19.
bowles-def-noncontextual-multitask-model: Definition 3.2 (printed 3.0), Section 3, p.10-11: noncontextual iff the associated scenario admits a noncontextual ontological model; contextual otherwise.
bowles-def-contextuality-applies-to-trai: Section 3, p.10: the definition applies to a trained h(theta), not the model class; footnote 6 says class-level definitions differ.
bowles-problem-linear-bias-setup: Problem 4.0/4.1, Section 4.1, p.11, Eq. 25 to 26: data with labels in {-1,1}^m, linear constraint on expected labels, sample the marginals for unseen x.
bowles-theorem-4-1: Theorem 4.1, p.13, with its conditions (m = 3, bias, V2/3 strictly inside conv V). Proved in Section 4.3 (Lemma 4.1 and Eq. 59, p.15 to 17) and in Appendix B for eta = 1.
bowles-theorem-4-1-contrapositive-expres: Section 4.1, p.13: the contrapositive of Theorem 4.1, followed by the paper's reading as a limit on noncontextual classes; the logic is immediate from the theorem.
bowles-operational-equivalence-effects-e: Section 4.2, Eq. 36 to 39, p.14: derived from the bias (28) by direct calculation (probabilities 1/2 for every preparation).
bowles-lemma-4-1-noncontextuality-inequa: Lemma 4.1, p.15: stated with its conditions and proved with a pen-and-paper argument on p.15 to 17 (Eq. 45 to 58).
bowles-lemma-4-1-violation-gives-theorem: Section 4.3, Eq. 59, p.17: the left side of (44) equals (3/2)(eta+1), which exceeds 5/2 for eta > 2/3; this finishes the proof of Theorem 4.1.
bowles-appendix-b-proof-eta-1: Appendix B, p.36-37: proof of Theorem 4.1 for eta = 1 (response functions deterministic, contradicting Eq. 127). The value's 'zero-noise' is the reader's label; the paper says eta = 1.
bowles-rps-game-setup: Section 5.1, p.17: three-player RPS game with a referee and probabilistic payoffs. Note E[Y(k)] = l_k(a)/2 in Eq. 60, so the value's 'given by' means up to the factor one half.
bowles-rps-zero-sum-bias: Section 5.2, p.18-19, Eq. 67: the paper's data distribution satisfies the zero-sum bias, by the zero-sum property of the game.
bowles-rps-learning-problem-definition: Problem 5.0/5.1, Section 5.3, p.19: the learning problem is defined by the paper.
bowles-rps-noncontextual-cannot-sample-a: Section 5.3, p.19: a direct application of Theorem 4.1 to the RPS problem; the strategies near the six deterministic ones give the extremal behaviours (eta = 1). Short corollary stated in the paper.
bowles-def-noncontextual-relative-to-bia: Definition 6.0/6.1, Section 6.2, p.21: noncontextual relative to a bias via the scenario restricted to the effects in the bias.
bowles-state-based-approach-conditions: Section 7.1, Eq. 84 to 86, p.22-23: bias-invariant unitaries are defined as the group G (Eq. 84); its Lie algebra is stated as the Hermitian operators commuting with H. A definition plus an elementary consequence.
bowles-state-based-no-general-input-prep: Section 7.1, p.23: 'We are unaware of general methods to construct parameterised unitaries in G'; ad-hoc methods used.
bowles-measurement-based-trine-and-limit: Section 7.2, p.24: trine example for a qubit, 'to the best of our knowledge' none for larger dimension, and Appendix D gives the m = 3 even-dimension construction.
bowles-appendix-d-even-dimension-constru: Appendix D, p.38: Eq. 128 to 130 derive (P-Q)^2 = (3/4) I and give block-form P and Q. The paper calls the check straightforward; I checked that P and Q are projections and (P-Q)^2 = 3/4 I.
bowles-biased-quantum-model-setup: Sections 8.1 to 8.2, Figure 7, p.25: three-qubit model, H = sum of sigma_z, state-based approach, RPS data set of 1500 strategies.
bowles-surrogate-model-setup: Section 8.3, p.26-27: surrogate is Fourier features models with the quantum frequency spectrum, with HardTanh; it does not encode the bias and the authors could not find a general method.
bowles-training-evaluation-setup: Section 8.4, p.28: NLL with Adam, KL divergence on 10000 sampled strategies; the training method is stated not to scale.
bowles-no-quantum-advantage-claim: Section 8, p.24: the authors state they do not claim quantum advantage because the models are easily simulated on a laptop.
bowles-zero-sum-larger-payoff-operationa: Section 9.1, p.29: the equivalence is derived (Eq. 104 to 106) and the paper says a clear picture of how the constraints affect learning is still needed.
bowles-extensions-single-model-not-class: Section 9.4, p.30: the authors state the framework is not the only option nor the most general, and name transformations and class-level definitions as extensions.
bowles-open-classical-encoding: Section 10, p.31: the authors name as the most pertinent open question whether such conserved quantities can be encoded in classical models with tractable resources.

theory_low.thm-iii-4-statement: Theorem III.4 is stated with its conditions (Section III A, p.6). The paper itself says the proof is only partly carried out: Appendix E 2 treats one additive contribution of the energy in full, and the other contributions and the second moments are 'sketched' (end of E 2, Appendix F intro and F 2). Not a full proof in the paper, so not the proved-result basis.
theory_low.thm-iii-4-uniform-in-n: Remark after Theorem III.4 (p.6); a consequence of the error bound. It rests on Theorem III.4, whose proof is partial (one contribution in full, the rest sketched).
theory_low.thm-iii-4-w-high-probability: Rests on Propositions F.15 and F.17 plus Theorem III.4. F.15 uses the second-moment estimates of F.14, which are sketched; F.17 is proved only as 'essentially repeating' F.15.
theory_low.main-technical-insight: The authors' own characterization ('surprisingly', 'main technical insight', Section I A, p.3). The equivalence of the two limits rests on Theorem III.4, whose proof is partial. An interpretation, not a proved statement.
theory_low.technical-overview-n-independent-order: Figure 4 caption, overview sentence: 'can be shown' to be independent of n. The supporting proofs are in Appendices D to F and are partly sketched. Not a stated-and-proved result at this location.
theory_low.prop-e5-noninteracting-correlations: Proposition E.5 is stated for all d. The proof (p.93-94) is written for d = 2 only; 'the generalization to arbitrary d is straightforward from the proof' is not written out. Borderline: the formula is elementary and the d = 2 case is complete.
theory_low.prop-f15-concentration: Proposition F.15 (p.146) is proved by Chebyshev from the second-moment estimates of Proposition F.14. Those estimates come from the contributions that Appendix F 2 only sketches ('we sketch how a similar analysis would work'), and 'sufficiently small' is not made explicit. So the proof is not complete in the paper.
theory_low.prop-f17-concentration-qa: Proposition F.17 (p.149) has no proof of its own: 'by essentially repeating the proof of Proposition F.15'. F.15 rests on sketched estimates. The printed statement also repeats the QAOA expressions.
theory_low.trotter-standard-requires-1-over-n: Section III D, p.15-16: an argument from the cited standard Trotter error bound and the norm scaling of the Hamiltonians (constraints 98 and 104). Argued in prose from a cited bound, not a theorem the paper states and proves.
theory_low.corollary-iii-5-quadratic-depth: Corollary III.5 (p.16): its short proof rests on Theorem III.4 (partial proof) and on the prose claim that the standard analysis needs n layers. Also 'with high probability' relies on the concentration propositions.
theory_low.qaoa-qa-conditions: The new value is the more exact (conditions plus the disorder-average SK scope). But it says the paper proves it, and the proof of Theorem III.4 is partial (one contribution in full, the rest sketched; see thm-iii-4-statement). The stored HIGH should be reviewed by the team lead.
theory_low.qaoa-qa-equivalence-proof: The new value adds the Lipschitz and small-gamma conditions of Theorem III.4 and is the better value. The proof is only partly carried out in the paper (one additive contribution in full, others sketched, App E 2 and F), so the proved-result basis fails. The stored HIGH should be reviewed by the team lead.
theory_low.bowles-operational-equivalence-preparati: Section 4.2, Eq. 40 to 43, p.14: the derivation holds only under the hypothesis that the hull of V contains the six points u_i(eta) for some eta > 2/3 (from strict containment of V2/3). The value and quotes drop that condition.
theory_low.bowles-joint-model-full-scenario-may-mis: Section 6.1, p.20-21: a motivating argument for Definition 6.1, illustrated by an example in Appendix C. It says contextuality 'may' be unprovable. Not a theorem or proposition. Borderline: the example is explicit but brief.
theory_low.bowles-appendix-a-theory-as-scenario-pro: Appendix A, p.35-36: the authors' argument for a design choice. The mathematical point (no preparation equivalences, so no contextuality) has a one-line construction, but the claim that contextuality then depends on irrelevant physical details is interpretation.

value_replace.bowles-operational-equivalence-preparati: The paper derives that, for preparation densities s1 to s6 realizing the six points u_i(eta) for some eta greater than 2/3 (which exist because V_2/3 lies strictly inside the convex hull of V), equally mixing the pairs (s1, s2), (s3, s4) and (s5, s6) each gives a preparation returning uniformly random labels for the three tasks, so the three mixtures are operationally equivalent.
